description: Fix compose.yaml production NODE_ENV from development to production

asi.hypothesis: Fix NODE_ENV from 'development' to 'production' in compose.yaml - the production Docker Compose file was accidentally running the app in development mode, affecting framework behavior and error handling.
asi.insight: A subtle but important bug. Production Docker Compose deployments were running the Hono/Better Auth app in NODE_ENV=development, which can enable debug endpoints, verbose error messages, and disable production optimizations.

description: Pass RESEND_API_KEY and RESEND_FROM environment variables to app container in compose.yaml

asi.hypothesis: The deploy workflow writes RESEND_API_KEY and RESEND_FROM to .env, but compose.yaml doesn't pass them to the app container. sendMagicLinkEmail.ts reads them from process.env at runtime, so magic link emails would fail silently in production Docker deployments.
asi.insight: A production deployment bug: RESEND_API_KEY and RESEND_FROM were written to .env by the deploy script but never passed through to the app service's environment block in compose.yaml. This meant the sendMagicLinkEmail function would throw in production because RESEND_API_KEY would be undefined inside the container.

description: Replace waitFor polling with deterministic microtask flushing in heavy jsdom tests

asi.hypothesis: Several slow jsdom tests only wait for immediately resolved fetch promises and local state updates. Replacing waitFor polling with a tiny act-based microtask flush should preserve assertions while reducing test overhead.
asi.insight: The three targeted files dropped from about 1.50s to 1.40s locally, and full just check improved from 3.6s to 3.5s. Assertions still cover the same post-fetch UI and callback behavior, but without polling loops.
asi.safety_note: Only tests changed; production behavior and benchmark semantics were unchanged.

description: Remove the last waitFor polling loops from logs-viewer and dashboard jsdom tests

asi.hypothesis: The last remaining waitFor uses in jsdom tests are microtask-only UI updates, not real timer/backoff behavior. Replacing them with deterministic act-based microtask flushing should shave a bit more overhead off just check without weakening coverage.
asi.insight: No waitFor calls remain in src test files now. The targeted suites (logs-viewer and the initial dashboard error-state test) still assert the same post-fetch UI, and full just check improved from 3.5s to 3.4s.
asi.safety_note: Only tests/docs changed; production code and benchmark semantics were unchanged.

description: Tried removing explicit RTL cleanup calls, but this Vitest setup does not auto-clean between tests

asi.hypothesis: @testing-library/react may already auto-run cleanup after each test, so removing explicit cleanup() calls from jsdom test files could reduce repeated DOM teardown overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: This project does not expose the test runner lifecycle to Testing Library's auto-cleanup hook in a way that replaces the explicit cleanup() calls. Removing them left DOM state shared across tests, causing duplicate-role and duplicate-text failures.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep explicit cleanup() in RTL tests here and look for a different low-risk runtime optimization, such as reducing jsdom suite setup cost or import overhead instead of removing required teardown.
asi.failure_mode: cross-test DOM leakage caused multi-match Testing Library failures in several jsdom suites
asi.insight: In this setup, imported vitest afterEach hooks are not enough for @testing-library/react's implicit cleanup path to safely replace explicit cleanup() in the test files.

description: Switch jsdom tests to @testing-library/react/pure imports

asi.hypothesis: Importing @testing-library/react/pure in jsdom test files may avoid some module-level setup overhead while preserving the same render/cleanup semantics with explicit cleanup calls.
asi.rollback_reason: The full just check run regressed from 3.4s to 3.7s, so the pure-import swap did not help the real benchmark despite looking plausible in a targeted subset run.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep standard RTL imports and explore a different low-risk path, such as reducing jsdom component render cost or test import overhead in the heaviest suites.
asi.insight: A targeted subset passed, but full-suite transform/import time increased enough to make the overall benchmark slower. The alternate entrypoint likely offers no net advantage in this Vitest setup.

description: Mock lucide-react icons with a tiny test-only module in Vitest

asi.hypothesis: Many jsdom-tested components import several lucide-react icons. Replacing the icon library with a tiny test-only SVG mock should reduce transform/import/render overhead while preserving text-based assertions and interactions.
asi.rollback_reason: The full just check benchmark regressed from the current 3.4s best to 3.5s, so the icon-mocking setup did not improve the real target even though targeted jsdom suites got faster.
asi.next_action_hint: Leave real lucide imports in place and look for optimizations outside decorative icon mocking, such as reducing heavy component setup in the slowest suites or improving non-jsdom import costs.
asi.targeted_signal: The eight jsdom suites improved in isolation, but the full-suite result did not beat the current best.
asi.insight: A global test-only alias can help a focused subset while still losing overall once configuration overhead and the rest of the suite are included.
